pages.text: Formats a value as text with a format string.

Conversions start with $(1)%$(), e.g. $(1)%5d$() (integer, 5 wide), $(1)%.2f$() (2 decimal places), $(1)%s$() (any value), $(1)%tF$() and $(1)%tT$() (date and time). A wrong type raises TYPE_MISMATCH, a bad format string INVALID_ARGUMENT.

All conversions use the same value, so one value can feed several of them: $(1)"%tF %tT"$() shows date and time, and $(1)"%d = 0x%X"$() turns 255 into $(1)255 = 0xFF$(). For two values, call FORMAT twice and join the texts with $(1)⊕$().
$(1)%f$(), $(1)%e$() and $(1)%g$() take INTEGERs and FLOATs. $(1)%d$(), $(1)%x$() and $(1)%o$() only take INTEGERs, so round a FLOAT first with ROUND or INT of c0de/math.

The text is always English, whatever language the game or the server uses: $(1).$() is the decimal point, $(1),$() the thousands separator ($(1)%,d$() turns 1234567 into $(1)1,234,567$()), and the names of weekdays and months are English ($(1)%tA$() gives $(1)Monday$()). The $(1)%t$() codes use the time zone of the server.
$(li)$(1)value$() BOOLEAN|INTEGER|FLOAT|CHAR|STRING|TIME: the value$(li)$(1)format$() STRING: the format string$(li)result $(1)result$() STRING: the formatted text
$(1)CALL c0de/strings/FORMAT$(br)  PARAMETER value now ;$(br)  PARAMETER format "%tF %tT" ;$(br)  RESULT result text$()
